killed.because: Kill prong 1, leakage: the mint law admits questions answerable without the corpus through the auto-loaded boot context, and no instrument the spec names can see that channel. Its span classes include exact error strings; the checks file shows AGENTS.md contains the error string 'No module named' (S4) and every harness seat receives AGENTS.md injected by default (this judging session's own context carries it). No named screen covers boot files: the span-uniqueness oracle treats a boot file as ordinary bytes so a boot-held span can be the unique holder and pass; the path/title exclusion only reads catalog row path/title, and the repo AGENTS.md currently has no catalog row at all (S1), so that screen cannot even see the file; the map-only check and Arm M test map leakage, not context leakage; the corpus-blind probe either runs without boot content (raw model, blind to the channel) or voids only at 2+ correct, which ships a single leaked question under the card's 'any question' law. The spec itself names 'prompting' inside its adversary model yet screens nothing over the prompt-included file set. Corroborating but not the kill basis: exactly-one span uniqueness is evidenced only on a 1,978-file slice while corpus-scale echoes are pervasive (S5 spot checks: 'B2-186' in 9 files, 'SEED_SELF_STEAL_AUDIT_20260926.md' in 9 including COMPASS.md and both briefs, 'a54ff182c7e8' in 9 including pytest fixtures, '12.352s' in 4). Its B2-186 leak diagnosis, zone table, and vault placement were all verified sound (S1, S3, S6); it dies on the screen gap, not the diagnosis.

ruling: uf122-two lives because its mint law mechanically excludes every channel the kill condition names (boot-file screen S4 plus the per-run miner blind arm for leakage, loopback-only ollama verified live with gemma:2b present for the network prong, and an operator-custodied vault outside both the walk root and repo confinement with salted commitments for held-out discipline), while uf122-one dies on the leakage prong because its named span classes intersect the auto-injected boot set and none of its screens can detect that channel.
critique: Post-run gold-path rot: grader verdicts and in-repo status publish 12-hex catalog ids, and catalog.jsonl itself maps id to path for every row (tools/corpus.py:101-102 derives them from paths), so the ids are trivially invertible in-repo and every condition-B re-run after the first baseline evaluates a miner that can read prior gold paths; add a gold-rot policy (re-mint cadence for scored runs, or aggregate-only receipts until the operator verification window opens).

Order the defenses explicitly: the per-run miner blind arm is the load-bearing leakage enforcement and the janitor closed-book probe (S8) is only a tripwire, since gemma:2b, verified present this session, is unlikely to blind-solve estate trivia; the landed spec must say which defense carries the kill condition.

Mint-block dependency handling: S8 hard-requires a responding local ollama at 127.0.0.1:11434; specify refusal semantics (mint exits 2 naming the unreachable endpoint, never silently skips the screen) so an ollama outage cannot produce an unscreened mint.
Span-growth termination budget: S2's monotone span growth needs a max span length and a max growth-attempt count per candidate so the mint terminates in bounded time on pathological candidates.

Seal-time audit surface: record per-stratum pool counts and settling-set size distribution next to the commitments so the |S| <= 5 budget is auditable at seal, and record the vault-creation event so an absent C:/Users/foste/.mag_eval/uf122/ (verified absent this session, S3) reads as not-yet-minted rather than lost gold.

Keep the settling-set correction of the lane prompt's 'answerable ONLY by one specific file' explicit in the landed spec with the echo evidence cited (judge-verified echoes: 7-of-7 hand-picked spans failed uniqueness per the candidate's full-pool scans, corroborated by this session's spot checks at 4 to 9 files per needle), so a later reader does not re-tighten to exactly-one without new measurements.
